name: Junghwan Yim
affiliation: Ph.D. Student · Georgia Institute of Technology
bio_html: I am a second-year Ph.D. student in Mechanical Engineering at the Georgia Institute of Technology. My research connects robotics, manufacturing, agentic AI, digital twins, and cybersecurity to help autonomous systems build and maintain a trustworthy understanding of the physical world.

I believe that observing reality and understanding its state are the starting points for meaningful innovation. My passion for digital twins comes from the ambition to represent the physical world digitally, including its changing conditions, interactions, and uncertainty. Without grounding in observation, visions of autonomy remain speculation rather than science.

My research focuses on adaptive and secure agentic digital twins: systems that continuously observe physical environments, estimate their state, and update their models as conditions change. I investigate how these representations can remain reliable despite uncertainty, limited computation, and compromised information, enabling AI and robots to make better decisions.

This direction is grounded in hands-on experience supporting the design, construction, and automation of BlueOval SK’s Ford–SK On battery manufacturing facilities in the United States. Having applied AI to practical engineering problems, I aim to develop methods that work beyond the laboratory. I work across disciplines, continually asking what we need to understand, which methods are missing, and how research can lead to working solutions.
interests: Adaptive state estimation: how can a digital twin stay aligned with a changing physical environment?
Efficient observation and simulation: what should a system measure or simulate next under limited resources?
Trustworthy autonomy: how can agents detect stale or compromised state information and make reliable decisions?
